subject: 'Strong condemnation' for China, 'apologise' at home
alt: Cartoon: under a grey-lilac sky, a dark silhouette-like figure in a cap stands at left, pointing with one hand and saying: 'Chinese folks, our Defence Minister is busy with something important right now. He will come later and strongly condemn you! Be careful!' At right is a green tank with 'Defence Minister' written on its side; in place of a turret it carries the large head of a bald, scowling man, and the tank's long gun barrel comes out where his nose would be. He thunders: 'Insult to Modiji's father...! Apologise...!' The cartoonist's signature is at the bottom left.
chutki: The tank marked 'Defence Minister' has its muzzle set like a gun barrel, and its target is 'the insult to Modiji's father'. Meanwhile the man at left is explaining to those across the border that the minister is busy with something very important and will come later to 'strongly condemn' them. The gun, in other words, is turned inwards, and for outsiders there is only a promise: condemnation is certain, the date is not.

Dhodapkar's jab lies in exactly this split. If even a part of the roar kept in reserve for demanding apologies at home were available at the border, words like 'strong condemnation' might have stayed in the dictionary. Here the tank is the minister and the minister is the tank; the only difference is that everyone already knows who is 'busy' when it matters.
